title: From reconstruction to reasoning : neural radiance fields for comprehensive 3D scene understanding
abstract: Embodied artificial intelligence requires agents that can perceive, navigate, understand, and act upon user-defined tasks within complex environments. Achieving this demands a perceptual system that can bridge the gap between the reconstruction precision and the semantic richness respectively required for control and reasoning. This thesis proposes that Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) can serve as the foundation for such a system, evolving from their original role as a view-synthesis tool into a robust, queryable scene map that anchors a modular embodied ecosystem.We first address the foundational need for a reliable, in-the-wild geometric mapping, introducing RING-NeRF. This architecture integrates structural inductive biases to solve the robustness gaps of standard NeRFs, enabling stable, incremental and adaptive reconstruction from sparse or imperfect multi-view imagery. Building upon this, we enable the agent's self-functioning capabilities by developing direct interpretation methods. We propose architectural enhancements and generalization techniques to perform semantic segmentation directly within the NeRF model, providing the fixed-category understanding essential for navigation and object manipulation.Finally, we address the challenge of open-ended, user-driven scene understanding. We first introduce DiSCO-3D, an open-vocabulary NeRF segmentation framework that allows the agent to focus locally and decompose specific concepts based on arbitrary text queries. Complementing this local understanding, we develop LLaVA³, a global reasoning pipeline that interfaces the 3D NeRF representation with Large Vision-Language Models, enabling the agent to interpret the environment holistically and plan complex tasks without fine-tuning of the foundation model.Through these contributions, the thesis establishes a comprehensive framework where a robust, semantically grounded NeRF serves as the central state representation, supporting specifically designed modules for both the functional reflexes and the cognitive reasoning of an embodied agent.
